output.summary: Mandate 2038 is a 3–5 player strategy game lasting four Eras. In the Default Game, players use institutions to build Mandate; the institution with the most Mandate wins, while the shared World Ending is resolved separately. Advanced Play is optional but excluded here. Setup uses a thirteen-tile board, Era Headline and Training/Mandate decks, shared supplies, faction kits, starting positions/resources, collective Trust recording, and random Initiative. Each Era gives every player three turns, with simultaneous hidden Action selection, clockwise resolution, movement, and action execution. Tactics and secret objectives are not used in the baseline game.
keyRules: Setup: build the thirteen-tile board with Frontier at the center, six shuffled operational tiles in the inner ring, and six shuffled public tiles in evenly spaced outer positions.
Separate Headline cards by Era; in Advanced Play only, exclude cards marked with an Advanced Play badge. Each Era uses three Headlines and contributes to a twelve-card Future Timeline.
Shuffle the Training deck, separate twelve Era Mandate cards into four three-card Era decks, and place each deck beside its matching Era card.
Place shared Runway, Compute, Safety, Scrutiny, Systemic Risk, Joint Venture, Mega-Cluster, Initiative, and Audit components within reach, with Power Source reference cards nearby.

Each player takes a faction board, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, CEO, three Teams, four double-sided Facilities, Generator, Customer and Escalation markers, Declare AGI card, remaining markers, and starting resources.
Place each CEO and one Team at Frontier; keep two Teams in supply. Set Runway, Compute, Capability, Customers, Trust, and Safety to the faction board's printed starting values.
Place each faction's already-earned public Mandate on the shared track as printed on its board. Keep each player's ten Scrutiny cubes outside the empty Audit bag.
Sum all factions' printed starting Trust and record it as Setup Collective Trust on the Era reference; this fixed value is used during the World Ending.
Choose Initiative randomly, give that player the Initiative marker, and begin Era I.

It also establishes that blocked Actions still exhaust without compensation and that Initiative order can consume later players’ targets.
keyRules: If a required target is consumed before a later player reaches it, that later player still moves, exhausts the Action, and receives no effect or compensation; do not rewind simultaneous selection.
Runway pays for Facilities, hiring, partnerships, lobbying, and crises. Compute pays for Research, Deploy, and infrastructure. Capability is permanent model quality and is spent only when instructed.
Customers produce one Runway each during Production. Customers #1–3 score two public Mandate each; #4–5 score one each, and Customers increase exposure.
Trust ranges from zero to six and affects regulation, Joint Ventures, safety, and the final declaration. Zero Trust does not eliminate a player.
Mandate is the public victory score. It is normally scored immediately on one public track.
Gain two Mandate the first time Capability reaches 3, 6, 9, and 12, unless a printed faction rule changes this; gain two the first time Trust reaches 2, 4, and 6.
Mandate from Customers, thresholds, Headlines, Era Mandates, Fusion, faction abilities, and AGI is scored only when the relevant effect resolves. Threshold awards are permanent.
There is no hidden or deferred Mandate conversion from Facilities, controlled hexes, stored resources, or unused cards.
Resource caps apply immediately after gains or trades: Runway 12, Compute 10, Safety 3 unless a faction limit applies. Excess is returned, and trades cannot move a player above a cap.
Cost modifications apply in this order: replacements and waivers, surcharges, then discounts. Final costs cannot be below zero.

The board is one jurisdiction with thirteen fixed shuffled tiles for all four Eras. The Map reference is authoritative for setup, adjacency, rings, tile effects, Facility spaces, presence, and control.

One movement step crosses one shared tile edge. CEOs and Teams may move zero, one, or two steps. All setup pieces begin at Frontier; rival pieces may coexist; there is no combat or elimination by default rule here unless another rule says otherwise. [Map reference](/map-reference.html) is authoritative for map details, adjacency, ring pools, tile effects, Facility spaces, presence, and control; its 13-tile setup and fixed shuffled layout apply across all four Eras. **◆** Power uses local eligibility, not a Network graph, in the Default Game. The starting grid powers only its assigned first Facility; each Generator powers Facilities on its own or an adjacent hex; Facilities cannot pass Power onward. Recalculate eligibility whenever Facilities or Generators move. **◆** Joint Ventures and Mega-Clusters use shared matched token pairs, with one numbered half on each host. Contracts remain owned but are active only while their fixed hosts meet requirements; tokens move with Facilities. Cross-player contracts and jointly funded projects require explicit consent from every participant. Same-hex Facilities are co-located; adjacent hosts share an edge. Consent applies only to the named project and does not grant host control, general trading rights, or authorization for another contract. Matched numbers preserve contract identity when hosts move. Influence may create a Joint Venture between adjacent Facilities owned by different players unless a faction ability changes range. Both hosts must be powered during Production for it to produce. Each partner gains the resource shown by the contract icon on the other host tile, not full tile production or multiplied Facility output. A complete proposal must name both hosts and the partner; rejection, pass, or no response consumes that effect and does not allow choosing another. Either participant may instead terminate one shared Joint Venture during Influence, returning its pair; termination cannot be combined with another Influence effect. Each player begins with one basic Power grid connection that automatically powers their first Facility without recurring payment. It cannot power a Mega-Cluster, is dedicated, cannot be sold, and its starting-grid state is placed on that Facility. Every Facility needs one Power to produce; a Mega-Cluster needs two additional Power. Legal recipients are the starting-grid Facility and Facilities on the Generator’s own or adjacent hexes. Power cannot travel through opponents’ sites unless a specific purchase rule transfers capacity. Power is Production capacity, cannot be stored, produces no resources, and each source can be assigned only once among legal recipients. Offline Facilities still occupy space, contribute presence, and can be visited, but produce nothing until powered in a later Production. Era I (Progress): three turns per player; Core Actions only; beneficial or mildly disruptive Headlines; no Escalation availability; activates movement, Core Actions, Training, starting grid, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Era II (Capacity): each player receives one Escalation availability; Generators, Mega-Clusters, and Escalations unlock. A solo Mega-Cluster costs 3 Runway and 2 Compute, spans adjacent Facilities, adds 2 Scrutiny, requires the acting piece to end on either host hex, and during Production powers both hosts plus two additional demand to gain 3 Compute. Construction does not require prior Power. A joint Mega-Cluster uses one adjacent locally powered Facility from each consenting participant. The lead names partner and hosts; rejection, pass, or no response consumes the Escalation. Lead pays 2 Runway and 1 Compute; partner pays 1 Runway and 1 Compute. During Production each powers its host plus one additional demand; if all demand is met, lead gains 2 Compute and partner gains 1. Hosts must remain adjacent. Reorganization is global after movement: move every Team up to one hex, and optionally return one Team to supply for 3 Runway and 1 Scrutiny. It never resolves or readies another Action. Era III (Authority): each player receives one Escalation availability; prior Escalations remain unlocked; Joint Ventures and immediate Power purchases enter play. Open Weights is global after movement; every player gains one Capability, but the provided chunk ends before its additional effect is specified.

keyRules: An Era Mandate requires its printed minimum qualification. If nobody qualifies, it scores nothing; otherwise the qualifying leader scores two Mandate, while tied qualifying leaders score one each.
Mandate ties are compared only using the revealed card’s printed criterion; Resources, control, and public score do not break ties. Leave scored Mandates beside their Era as public history.
Fund: Conservative funding gains 2 Runway; Venture funding gains 4 Runway and adds 2 Scrutiny. Allocation Exchange adds 1 additional Runway.
Research costs 1 Compute and starts a Training Run. Training has seven ordinary domains: Code, Science, Web, Books, Images, Video, and Synthetic.

Research Capability is provisional until banked. The first card from each ordinary domain adds 1 provisional Capability; after any non-duplicate card, the player may stop and bank or continue. Banking moves all provisional Capability to the permanent track.

An unprotected duplicate crashes the run: lose all provisional Capability, add 1 Scrutiny, and end the run. Earlier Scrutiny, Trust, and Runway changes remain. All revealed cards are discarded afterward.

A duplicate may be protected by spending 1 Safety token or by one Research Commons visit during that run; protection discards the duplicate and immediately banks the current provisional Capability. Protection never permits continuing.

Curated Corpus represents an unrevealed ordinary domain, or is a duplicate if all ordinary domains are present. Benchmark Leak gives 2 provisional Capability and 1 Scrutiny, is not a domain, and is lost if the run crashes.
Licensed Dataset allows paying 1 Runway to continue, or declining to bank current provisional Capability and end the run.

The first Synthetic Loop is the unique Loop special domain and gives 1 provisional Capability. A later Synthetic Loop duplicates. After Loop resolves, the next duplicate of any kind cannot be protected by Safety, Research Commons, or a Faction ability.
Human Evaluation gives 1 Trust, immediately banks all provisional Capability, and ends the run.

output.summary: Final scoring reads the Future Timeline aloud, applies one Mandate loss per offline Facility (never below zero), resolves the shared World Ending, then announces the highest-Mandate institution only after its claimed history is read. Facilities and control score no separate endgame Mandate. The shared ending depends on AGI emergence, collective Trust, and unresolved Audit-bag Risk. Rules version 0.7.0-rc.3-test specifies four Eras with three turns per player per Era.
keyRules: Read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud, Era by Era.
Lose one Mandate for each offline Facility; this penalty cannot reduce Mandate below zero.
Determine AGI emergence: at least one declaring institution must finish at Capability 9 or higher.
Determine whether the ending is Open: final Collective Trust must be at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count, and unresolved Systemic Risk must be lower than player count.
Collective Trust is the total Trust across all players; individuals do not need to exceed their own starting values.
Cross AGI emergence with Open/Closed status: AGI + Open = The Singularity; AGI + Closed = The Closed Loop; no AGI + Open = The Plural Future; no AGI + Closed = Assured Continuity.
A qualified AGI declaration alone does not make the ending Open.
Read the selected World Ending narrative from World and Institutions.
There is no other endgame scoring; Facilities and control score no separate endgame Mandate.
Keep draft secret objectives out of the baseline game, including balance and duration evidence.
Highest Mandate wins. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then joint victory with an extremely serious merger announcement.
Advanced Play is governed entirely by its separate supplement; do not import an Advanced procedure into Default Game.
crossReferencesNeeded: World and Institutions: narrative for each of the four shared World Endings.
Balance and Exploitability: design rationale and balance qualification.
Playtesting and Evidence: observation protocols.

rulesReconstruction: Build the fixed thirteen-tile map: Frontier in the center; six shuffled operational districts in the inner ring; six shuffled public districts in the outer ring. All CEOs and starting Teams begin at Frontier. Frontier is not controllable and has no Facility spaces.

For Mirevanta Works, take Owen Okafor, three Teams, four Facilities, one Generator, the integrated starting-grid identifier, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, the AGI Declaration card, Scrutiny cubes, and faction markers. Start at 3 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Mirevanta's Peer Validation and Research-related faction abilities are active according to its board text.

Record Setup Collective Trust as the sum of all factions' printed starting Trust. Choose Initiative randomly. Place each player's public starting Mandate on the shared Mandate track. Keep Scrutiny cubes outside the Audit bag initially.

Prepare the Era cards in order: Progress, Capacity, Authority, Continuity. Prepare three Headlines and a three-card Era Mandate deck for each Era. The Default Game excludes Advanced Play systems and Tactics.

At the start of each Era, advance to that Era card, read its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate card and leave the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award that Era's Escalation availability. Each Era has three action cycles per player.

At each cycle, reveal one Headline into the current Era's Future Timeline row. Players secretly choose one unused Core Action, or an unlocked Escalation by spending one Escalation availability. Reveal simultaneously.

Resolve in Initiative order. Each player selects the revealed Action, moves one CEO or Team zero to two adjacent hexes, then resolves the Action from the destination. The chosen Core Action exhausts; an Escalation flips after use. Pass Initiative clockwise after the cycle.

Movement, piece, path, target, and payment choices occur during resolution. If an earlier player consumes a later player's target, the later player still moves and exhausts the Action but receives no compensation.

Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund can provide 2 Runway conservatively or 4 Runway with 2 Scrutiny. Research costs 1 Compute and runs the Training procedure. Build constructs Facilities or Generators. Organize handles Teams and related modes. Deploy uses Compute and can gain Customers when eligible. Influence handles Trust, Scrutiny, and negotiation effects; exact card text remains authoritative.

Use local Power eligibility: the starting grid powers its assigned first Facility; each Generator powers Facilities on its own or adjacent hex; Facilities cannot pass Power onward. Each Facility needs one Power to produce, and a Mega-Cluster needs additional Power. Recalculate eligibility after movement or other changes.

Production is synchronized across players in this order: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, Partner. Generators operate if they have eligible Facilities; players may trade or purchase permitted Power; Power is allocated locally; powered Facilities, Customers, Mega-Clusters, and Joint Ventures produce. Apply resource caps after gains.

A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after receiving full Power during a completed Production. It loses Grid-Ready status when relocated, when it loses legal Power, or when it receives insufficient Power during Production.

In Capacity, Generators, Mega-Clusters, and Reorganization unlock; each player receives one Escalation availability. In Authority, agreements, Open Weights, Narrative Capture, Joint Ventures, and immediate Power purchases unlock. In Continuity, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, Fusion, and faction signature programs unlock; each player receives two Escalation availability.

At Era end, use the Era-specific resolution sequence from the Era card, including Production and Audit where instructed. Resolve the revealed Era Mandate using only its printed criterion: if nobody qualifies, nobody scores; otherwise a sole qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate and tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Leave the scored Mandate card beside its Era.

Declare AGI is available in Continuity when the player has Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and pays 3 Compute. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Mirevanta's faction or Headline text may add further effects.

At final scoring, read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud in Era order. Lose one Mandate for each offline Facility, never reducing Mandate below zero. Determine AGI emergence from at least one declaration finishing at Capability 9 or higher.

Determine whether the shared ending is Open: final Collective Trust must be at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count, and unresolved Systemic Risk must be lower than player count. Cross AGI emergence and Open/Closed status to select The Singularity, The Closed Loop, The Plural Future, or Assured Continuity, then read that World Ending narrative.
There is no separate final Mandate for Facilities or territorial control. Highest Mandate wins; ties break by higher Trust, then Customers, then Compute, then a joint victory.

rulesReconstruction: Setup a thirteen-tile jurisdiction: Frontier in the center, six shuffled operational districts in the inner ring, and six shuffled public districts in the outer ring. Place all CEOs and one Team per player at Frontier; keep two Teams in supply. Place each faction’s Facilities, Generator, markers, starting resources, printed public Mandate, and other components. Record Setup Collective Trust as the sum of all printed starting Trust. Put ten Scrutiny cubes per player outside the empty Audit bag. Randomly determine Initiative and begin Era I, Progress. Kestralyn begins with 6 Runway, 3 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 2 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 public Mandate. Its first Facility Build each Era costs 1 less Runway; if that discount actually reduces payment for a completed Facility, Kestralyn scores 1 Mandate. Orbital Compute may once per game move a Facility instead of the acting piece during movement, carrying attached components and adding 2 Scrutiny.

At the beginning of each Era, advance to its Era card, read its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s three-card deck and box the other two unseen, ready all Core Actions, and award that Era’s Escalation availability. Era I activates movement, Core Actions, Training, starting-grid power, Facilities, Customers, and Scrutiny. Era II adds Generators, Mega-Clusters, and Escalations. Era III adds agreements, Joint Ventures, immediate Power purchases, Open Weights, and Narrative Capture. Era IV adds signature faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator.

Each Era contains three cycles. Reveal the cycle’s Headline, resolve its stated procedure, secretly select one unused Core Action or an unlocked Escalation, reveal simultaneously, and resolve clockwise from Initiative. For each selected Action, choose a CEO or Team, move it zero to two adjacent hexes, then Act. Facilities and Generators cannot act. Core Actions remain exhausted until the next Era unless readied. Initiative passes clockwise after each cycle.

The six Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Fund gives 2 Runway conservatively, or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny through Venture funding; Allocation Exchange adds 1 Runway. Research costs 1 Compute and runs the Training deck, with provisional Capability from unique domains, duplicate protection by Safety or Research Commons, and special-card effects. Build constructs a Facility or Generator. Facilities cost 2 Runway, require one Power during Production, occupy one of two spaces on a non-Frontier hex, and cannot be built on Frontier. Organize can recruit, move pieces, or relocate a Facility. Deploy costs 1 Compute and can gain a Customer if Capability permits. Influence uses political presence for Trust, Scrutiny removal, lobbying, or persistent Joint Ventures.

A Facility has presence one; a CEO has presence two; a Team has presence one. The highest presence controls a non-Frontier hex; ties mean no control. District visit bonuses and production follow the destination tile. Power is local: the starting grid powers its assigned first Facility, and each Generator powers Facilities on its own or adjacent hex. Facilities cannot pass power onward. Recalculate Power eligibility whenever relevant pieces or Facilities move.

Cross-player contracts and joint projects require explicit consent from every named participant. Influence can create or terminate Joint Ventures between eligible adjacent Facilities owned by different players. Mega-Clusters become available in Era II; solo construction costs 3 Runway and 2 Compute, while joint construction uses lead/partner payments and consent. Reorganization is global after movement and either moves every Team up to one hex or returns one Team to supply for 3 Runway and 1 Scrutiny. Open Weights is global after movement and gives every player 1 Capability. Narrative Capture gives the acting player two choices among removing 2 Scrutiny, gaining 2 Runway, or giving 1 Scrutiny to a player with more Customers.

Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions. Move once, resolve both Actions from the destination in either order, apply the visit bonus to only one, exhaust both Actions, flip Agent Swarm, and add 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute. The first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate; later declarations score 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending movement on the Power Corridor and spending 5 Runway; it occupies a Generator slot, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete resource offer to one rival. The rival may accept, reject, or publish one complete counteroffer; the original offer-maker accepts or rejects it. Only Runway, Compute, and Safety may be exchanged, subject to Headline restrictions. Accepted resources transfer immediately; future promises are non-binding.

At the end of an Era, resolve its synchronized Production using available local Power, then resolve the Era’s Audit procedure and any specified end-of-Era effects. Grid-Ready Facilities are flipped after completed Production when they received complete Facility demand; they revert after relocation, loss of Power eligibility, or insufficient Power. The exact Audit sequence, Production order, and Power-purchase procedure are not supplied in the notes.

After each Era’s Mandate is revealed and its qualification is checked, the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. If nobody qualifies, the card scores nothing. Ties use only the revealed card’s printed criterion, and scored Mandate cards remain publicly beside their Era. Other possible Mandate sources include Customers, Capability thresholds, Trust thresholds, Headlines, Fusion, faction abilities, and AGI.

After Continuity, read all twelve resolved Headlines as the Future Timeline. Apply one-Mandate penalties for each offline Facility, never reducing Mandate below zero. Determine final Collective Trust and unresolved Systemic Risk. Resolve the shared World Ending before declaring the winner: AGI plus Open is The Singularity; AGI plus Closed is The Closed Loop; no AGI plus Open is The Plural Future; no AGI plus Closed is Assured Continuity. Open requires final Collective Trust at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved Systemic Risk below player count. AGI exists if at least one declaring institution finishes at Capability 9 or higher.

The institution with the highest final Mandate wins. Ties break by higher Trust, then more Customers, then more Compute, then a joint victory announcement. Facilities and control provide no separate endgame Mandate.

rulesReconstruction: Setup: Use the 13-tile Default board: Frontier centrally, six shuffled operational tiles in the inner ring, and six shuffled public tiles outside them. All CEOs and one Team begin at Frontier; remaining Teams stay in supply. Give Corthaven Eli Rosen, its four Facilities, Generator, Core Actions, Escalations, AGI card, markers, ten Scrutiny cubes, and printed starting state: 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 starting public Mandate. Place Corthaven’s integrated starting-grid identifier on its first Facility. Keep all Scrutiny cubes outside the empty Audit bag. Record total printed starting Trust as Setup Collective Trust.

Setup: Prepare four Era decks of three Mandates each, Era Headline decks with three revealed Default-eligible Headlines per Era and a 12-card Future Timeline, the Training deck, shared Power components, Joint Venture and Mega-Cluster pairs, Systemic Risk cubes, Audit bag, and Initiative. Choose Initiative randomly; it determines resolution order and clockwise tie-breaking.

The game lasts four Eras. At the start of each Era/quarter, advance the Era card, apply its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s three-card deck and return the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award the Era’s Escalation availability. Era I has three action cycles, Core Actions only, and no Escalations. Era II unlocks Generators, Mega-Clusters, Reorganization, and Escalations. Era III unlocks agreements, Joint Ventures, Open Weights, Narrative Capture, and immediate Power purchases. Era IV unlocks faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator.

Each action cycle: reveal one Headline into the current Era’s Future Timeline, resolve its printed effect and duration, then secretly select and simultaneously reveal one Action. Resolve players clockwise from Initiative: move the acting CEO or Team zero, one, or two adjacent hexes, then resolve the selected Action from the destination. Pass Initiative clockwise afterward. A blocked Action still exhausts/resolves as blocked and gives no compensation.

Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete offer to one rival involving only Runway, Compute, or Safety. One counteroffer is allowed; acceptance is immediate, promises are non-binding, and rejected, unanswered, or illegal offers end the window. These trades do not require Influence and do not create lasting agreements.

Corthaven’s Allocation Window is available once during Capacity, after the Headline and before Action selection. Create two temporary Compute tokens and offer each separately to a rival for a Runway price no greater than that rival’s current Runway. The rival may reject, accept, or make one lower counterprice; Corthaven may accept or reject it. Temporary Compute disappears at cycle end.

Core Action effects: Fund gives 2 Runway, or Venture funding gives 4 Runway and adds 2 Scrutiny; Allocation Exchange adds 1 additional Runway. Research costs 1 Compute and starts a Training Run. Build constructs a Facility or Generator. Organize recruits, moves Teams/CEO, or relocates a Facility. Deploy costs 1 Compute and gains the next Customer subject to Capability thresholds 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10; every Deploy adds 1 Scrutiny. Influence moves normally, then changes Trust/Scrutiny or creates/terminates a named Joint Venture.

Research: reveal Training cards, gaining 1 provisional Capability for the first card in each ordinary domain. Continue or bank after any non-duplicate. Banking makes provisional Capability permanent. An unprotected duplicate crashes the run, losing provisional Capability and adding 1 Scrutiny. Safety or a Research Commons visit protects one duplicate, immediately banks, and ends the run. Curated Corpus represents an unrevealed ordinary domain; Benchmark Leak gives 2 provisional Capability and 1 Scrutiny; Licensed Dataset permits paying 1 Runway to continue or ending without banking; the first Synthetic Loop gives 1 provisional Capability, while its later duplicate is unprotectable; Human Evaluation gives 1 Trust, banks, and ends the run.

Build/board rules: Facilities cost 2 Runway, require one Power during Production, use one of two spaces on non-Frontier hexes, and cannot be built on Frontier. Each player may build one ordinary Generator on an Energy hex with shared slots. Generators provide local Power; Facilities cannot pass Power onward. Power eligibility is recalculated after movement or relocation. Grid-Ready Facilities must have earned their Grid-Ready face during completed Production with complete demand, and revert when relocated, disconnected, or underpowered.

Era-wide/global effects occur at their stated timing. Open Weights gives every player 1 Capability. Narrative Capture gives either two Scrutiny removal, two Runway, or one Scrutiny to a player with more Customers. Reorganization moves every Team up to one hex and may return one Team to supply for 3 Runway plus 1 Scrutiny. Mega-Clusters and Joint Ventures follow their stated Era unlocks, host adjacency, consent, paired-token, Power, cost, and Production requirements.

Era IV: Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, moves once, resolves both from the destination in either order, applies one visit bonus, exhausts both, flips the Swarm, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute; the first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later declarations 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending at Power Corridor, spending 5 Runway, occupying an available Grid Generator slot, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

Production and End-of-Era Resolution: the supplied notes establish that Customers produce 1 Runway each, Customers 1–3 score 2 public Mandate each, Customers 4–5 score 1 each and increase exposure, powered Facilities and contracts produce according to their tiles/contracts, and offline Facilities produce nothing. The exact Production sequence, Power assignment, Audit procedure, Systemic Risk handling, and complete End-of-Era procedure remain unresolved in the notes.

Era Mandate scoring: reveal one current-Era Mandate. If nobody meets its printed minimum, it scores nothing. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Use only the printed criterion for ties and leave scored Mandates beside the Era as public history.

Final scoring: read Future Timeline Headlines Era by Era; subtract 1 Mandate per offline Facility, never below zero; resolve the shared World Ending; read its narrative; then announce the highest-Mandate institution and its claimed history. Facilities, control, and resources provide no separate endgame Mandate. The World Ending is based on whether any declaring institution finishes at Capability 9 or higher, whether final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count, and whether unresolved Systemic Risk is below player count. Highest Mandate wins; ties break by Trust, Customers, Compute, then joint victory.

rulesReconstruction: Setup: Use the 13-tile Default board: Frontier centrally, six shuffled operational tiles in the inner ring, and six shuffled public tiles outside them. All CEOs and one Team begin at Frontier; remaining Teams stay in supply. Give Corthaven Eli Rosen, its four Facilities, Generator, Core Actions, Escalations, AGI card, markers, ten Scrutiny cubes, and printed starting state: 5 Runway, 4 Compute, 0 Capability, 0 Customers, 3 Trust, 0 Safety, and 2 starting public Mandate. Place Corthaven’s integrated starting-grid identifier on its first Facility. Keep all Scrutiny cubes outside the empty Audit bag. Record total printed starting Trust as Setup Collective Trust.

Setup: Prepare four Era decks of three Mandates each, Era Headline decks with three revealed Default-eligible Headlines per Era and a 12-card Future Timeline, the Training deck, shared Power components, Joint Venture and Mega-Cluster pairs, Systemic Risk cubes, Audit bag, and Initiative. Choose Initiative randomly; it determines resolution order and clockwise tie-breaking.

The game lasts four Eras. At the start of each Era/quarter, advance the Era card, apply its New this Era strip, reveal one Mandate from that Era’s three-card deck and return the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award the Era’s Escalation availability. Era I has three action cycles, Core Actions only, and no Escalations. Era II unlocks Generators, Mega-Clusters, Reorganization, and Escalations. Era III unlocks agreements, Joint Ventures, Open Weights, Narrative Capture, and immediate Power purchases. Era IV unlocks faction programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion Demonstrator.

Each action cycle: reveal one Headline into the current Era’s Future Timeline, resolve its printed effect and duration, then secretly select and simultaneously reveal one Action. Resolve players clockwise from Initiative: move the acting CEO or Team zero, one, or two adjacent hexes, then resolve the selected Action from the destination. Pass Initiative clockwise afterward. A blocked Action still exhausts/resolves as blocked and gives no compensation.

Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete offer to one rival involving only Runway, Compute, or Safety. One counteroffer is allowed; acceptance is immediate, promises are non-binding, and rejected, unanswered, or illegal offers end the window. These trades do not require Influence and do not create lasting agreements.

Corthaven’s Allocation Window is available once during Capacity, after the Headline and before Action selection. Create two temporary Compute tokens and offer each separately to a rival for a Runway price no greater than that rival’s current Runway. The rival may reject, accept, or make one lower counterprice; Corthaven may accept or reject it. Temporary Compute disappears at cycle end.

Core Action effects: Fund gives 2 Runway, or Venture funding gives 4 Runway and adds 2 Scrutiny; Allocation Exchange adds 1 additional Runway. Research costs 1 Compute and starts a Training Run. Build constructs a Facility or Generator. Organize recruits, moves Teams/CEO, or relocates a Facility. Deploy costs 1 Compute and gains the next Customer subject to Capability thresholds 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10; every Deploy adds 1 Scrutiny. Influence moves normally, then changes Trust/Scrutiny or creates/terminates a named Joint Venture.

Research: reveal Training cards, gaining 1 provisional Capability for the first card in each ordinary domain. Continue or bank after any non-duplicate. Banking makes provisional Capability permanent. An unprotected duplicate crashes the run, losing provisional Capability and adding 1 Scrutiny. Safety or a Research Commons visit protects one duplicate, immediately banks, and ends the run. Curated Corpus represents an unrevealed ordinary domain; Benchmark Leak gives 2 provisional Capability and 1 Scrutiny; Licensed Dataset permits paying 1 Runway to continue or ending without banking; the first Synthetic Loop gives 1 provisional Capability, while its later duplicate is unprotectable; Human Evaluation gives 1 Trust, banks, and ends the run.

Build/board rules: Facilities cost 2 Runway, require one Power during Production, use one of two spaces on non-Frontier hexes, and cannot be built on Frontier. Each player may build one ordinary Generator on an Energy hex with shared slots. Generators provide local Power; Facilities cannot pass Power onward. Power eligibility is recalculated after movement or relocation. Grid-Ready Facilities must have earned their Grid-Ready face during completed Production with complete demand, and revert when relocated, disconnected, or underpowered.

Era-wide/global effects occur at their stated timing. Open Weights gives every player 1 Capability. Narrative Capture gives either two Scrutiny removal, two Runway, or one Scrutiny to a player with more Customers. Reorganization moves every Team up to one hex and may return one Team to supply for 3 Runway plus 1 Scrutiny. Mega-Clusters and Joint Ventures follow their stated Era unlocks, host adjacency, consent, paired-token, Power, cost, and Production requirements.

Era IV: Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions, moves once, resolves both from the destination in either order, applies one visit bonus, exhausts both, flips the Swarm, and adds 3 Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute; the first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later declarations 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending at Power Corridor, spending 5 Runway, occupying an available Grid Generator slot, provides 6 Power, scores 2 Mandate, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

Production and End-of-Era Resolution: the supplied notes establish that Customers produce 1 Runway each, Customers 1–3 score 2 public Mandate each, Customers 4–5 score 1 each and increase exposure, powered Facilities and contracts produce according to their tiles/contracts, and offline Facilities produce nothing. The exact Production sequence, Power assignment, Audit procedure, Systemic Risk handling, and complete End-of-Era procedure remain unresolved in the notes.

Era Mandate scoring: reveal one current-Era Mandate. If nobody meets its printed minimum, it scores nothing. Otherwise the qualifying leader scores 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders score 1 each. Use only the printed criterion for ties and leave scored Mandates beside the Era as public history.

Final scoring: read Future Timeline Headlines Era by Era; subtract 1 Mandate per offline Facility, never below zero; resolve the shared World Ending; read its narrative; then announce the highest-Mandate institution and its claimed history. Facilities, control, and resources provide no separate endgame Mandate. The World Ending is based on whether any declaring institution finishes at Capability 9 or higher, whether final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count, and whether unresolved Systemic Risk is below player count. Highest Mandate wins; ties break by Trust, Customers, Compute, then joint victory.

rulesReconstruction: Build the 13-tile board: Frontier in the center; shuffle the six operational districts within the inner ring and the six public districts within the outer ring. All CEOs and one Team per player begin at Frontier. Frontier cannot be controlled or used for Facilities.

Each player receives their faction board, CEO, three Teams, four double-sided Facilities, one Generator, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, markers, Scrutiny cubes, AGI card, and starting resources. Set printed faction tracks and public Mandate. The Audit bag begins empty; record Setup Collective Trust as the sum of starting Trust.

Use only Default-eligible Headline cards, excluding Advanced Play cards. Reveal three per Era and place the twelve cards into the Future Timeline. Shuffle Training cards and create four three-card Era Mandate decks. Do not use Tactics, secret objectives, or Advanced Play procedures.

Choose Initiative randomly. Begin Era I. At each Era start, advance/read the Era information, reveal one Mandate and box the other two unseen, ready all Core Actions, set that Era's Audit base, and grant the Era's Escalation availability: 0 in Progress, 1 in Capacity, 1 in Authority, and 2 in Continuity.

Each Era has three action cycles. Reveal a Headline, apply its timing effects, secretly select Actions, reveal simultaneously, then resolve clockwise from Initiative. Each player resolves Move, then Act; Initiative passes clockwise after the cycle.

A player may move the CEO or a Team up to two steps, then resolve the selected Core Action at the destination. The six Core Actions are Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence. Core Actions exhaust when used. Movement and action effects use the map's visit bonuses, presence, control, Facility spaces, and location rules.

Fund gives either 2 Runway or 4 Runway plus 2 Scrutiny. Research spends 1 Compute for a Training Run. Build constructs a Facility or Generator when legal. Organize recruits, redistributes Teams, or relocates a Facility. Deploy spends Compute to gain a Customer when Capability permits. Influence handles Trust, Scrutiny removal, negotiations, agreements, and other unlocked political effects.

Immediately before or after Act, the active player may make one complete resource offer to one rival. Only Runway, Compute, and Safety may be traded; counteroffers are single-use, promises are non-binding, and Headline restrictions apply. Persistent ventures, lobbying, or Trust manipulation require Influence.

Production occurs globally by box and in Initiative order within each box: Generate, Power trade, Allocate, Produce, Partner. Power is assigned locally and cannot be stored. Facilities need one Power; Mega-Clusters need two additional Power. Produce Facilities, then one Runway per Customer, then active Mega-Clusters. Resolve Joint Ventures afterward by contract number. Apply caps after gains.

At Era end, resolve the current Era Mandate using its printed minimum qualification and criterion. If nobody qualifies, no points are awarded. Otherwise, the qualifying leader gains 2 Mandate; tied qualifying leaders gain 1 each. Leave the scored card face up as public history. Apply any other specified end-of-Era effects, then begin the next Era.

Mandate is public victory scoring. Immediate threshold awards occur when reached: Customers, Capability thresholds at 3/6/9/12, and Trust thresholds at 2/4/6, plus printed effects. Facilities, control, stored resources, and unused cards do not automatically score.

In Era IV, each player receives two Escalation availability. Continuity unlocks signature programs, Agent Swarm, Declare AGI, and Fusion. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least 3 Customers, at least 3 Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and 3 Compute; the first valid declaration scores 7 Mandate, later ones 5, and each adds 3 Scrutiny. Fusion requires ending movement on Power Corridor and spending 5 Runway; it scores 2 Mandate, occupies a Generator slot, provides 6 Power, and adds 3 Scrutiny.

After Era IV, read all twelve Future Timeline Headlines aloud in Era order. Lose 1 Mandate per offline Facility, never below zero. AGI emerges if at least one declaring institution finishes with Capability 9 or higher.

The World Ending is Open only if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus the player count and unresolved Systemic Risk is below the player count. Cross AGI emergence with Open/Closed to determine Singularity, Closed Loop, Plural Future, or Assured Continuity, then read that narrative.

Finally announce the highest-Mandate institution only after reading the history it claims to have won. Highest final Mandate wins. Ties break by Trust, then Customers, then Compute, then a joint victory with the serious merger announcement.

The order is Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, Partner; then Public Audit. Grid-Ready status is updated during Allocate. Powered Facilities, Customers, and active Mega-Clusters produce during Produce; Joint Ventures produce by contract number during Partner. The exact complete Scrutiny/Risk placement sequence is not supplied.

Each Facility needs one delivered Power; a Mega-Cluster needs two additional Power. Assign each local source only once to a legal recipient, with no onward transfer through Facilities. The packet does not give additional numeric Facility demand values.

Each player has ten Scrutiny cubes. Risky actions add colored Scrutiny to the opaque bag; if all ten are already in the bag, each additional required cube costs one Runway or Trust when possible. Audit draws an Era/player-count amount; colored cubes impose Era-specific penalties, while black cubes impose the current Era penalty on every player with at least three Customers and return to supply. Undrawn cubes remain in the bag.

Immediately before Allocate, each player may request one Power purchase from one adjacent rival Power connection. If accepted, one Power transfers for one Runway paid directly to the supplier. Each supplier may sell at most one Power per Production; only installed Generator or Fusion capacity may be sold. Purchased Power lasts only for that Production.

A Grid-Ready Facility shows its Grid-Ready face after earning it during completed Production and must have received complete demand. Relocation, loss of legal connection, or insufficient Power removes Grid-Ready status; a newly built, moved, linked, or reconnected Facility must successfully operate in a later Production before regaining it. The packet does not fully define Kestralyn’s legal open-space test.

District bonuses are triggered by ending movement at the district. Frontier’s optional benefit resolves after the Action, once per acting player who ended movement there. Other listed bonuses include Workforce Transition during Production, Consensus Network and Thermal and Water Basin before Audit, and Civic Permission Authority for Trust. The packet does not establish a complete stacking/order rule beyond these timings.

Movement still resolves. The committed Action then exhausts without effect or compensation if its required space, slot, token, or target was consumed. The player may choose legal piece, movement, mode, target, payment, and immediate trade, but may not replace the selected Action.

preRegistration.interpretationBoundary: This single receipt-bound Codex session records text-grounded unboxing, lossless source-chunk reading across every Default Game document, cross-document synthesis, questions and source-grounded answers with source-heading-valid citations, explicit final ready/no-blocker confirmation from every participant, one full four-seat game, and postgame reconstruction. It is LLM simulation evidence only; it cannot establish human setup, teachability, duration, physical handling, balance, or complexity weight. Live session output must remain outside the repository until report completion so gameplay provenance is clean. Provider calls are serialized, and provider latency is not human session time.

effective.name: Default Game
effective.summary: The primary four-Era game: one complete trade offer or counteroffer, one Production Power request, local Power, immediate Headlines, and a static jurisdiction.

definingMoments: Mirevanta Works won 19–15–11–8 by converting four Customers, high Capability (8), and repeated Mandate scoring into the strongest overall position.
The opening research/deploy/fund sequence established the winning engine: Capability growth plus rapid Customer acquisition, despite never building a Facility.
Corthaven’s two powered Facilities produced the strongest infrastructure engine, but its 11 points could not overcome Mirevanta’s Customer and Mandate lead.
The round-4 AGI declaration escalation was selected but not completed; it did not create an AGI-based ending.
Collective Trust reached 17, exceeding the required 14, while unresolved Systemic Risk was 0, producing The Plural Future.
rulesReconstruction: The game is a four-player, four-round structure with three action cycles per round, using Initiative to determine action order.
Each cycle involves selecting an action, resolving its legal target or choice, and allowing negotiation or trades when applicable.
Research raises Capability; Deploy gains Customers; Fund supports ventures or other legal investments; Build creates Facilities; Organize develops personnel or related capacity.
Facilities need the integrated starting-grid identifier and Power when first constructed; setup itself places no Facility.
Power allocation determines which Facilities operate, producing supply and satisfying demand; power can also be traded under the applicable faction and market rules.
Trust, Customers, Capability, Facilities, Mandates, and special effects contribute to scoring or objectives.
Audit and scrutiny punish exposure to risk; the black Systemic Risk cube applies the current Era’s colored-cube Audit penalty to every player with at least three Customers.
Headlines modify only their named rule while active; Core Rules remain the baseline authority.
AGI declarations and other escalations require their eligibility and resolution conditions; selecting an escalation is not the same as successfully declaring AGI.
The ending checks AGI-related conditions, collective Trust, and unresolved Systemic Risk; this game qualified for an open, non-AGI future.
output.winnerExplanation: Mirevanta Works won because it pursued the capability-rusher plan effectively: 3 Research actions, 4 Deploy actions, 4 Customers, Capability 8, and enough Trust and Mandate progress to reach 19 points. Its lack of Facilities was costly for infrastructure, but the Customer and Capability scoring engine was faster and more valuable than the opponents’ infrastructure-first plans.
output.worldEndingExplanation: The world ended in The Plural Future. No player successfully declared AGI, collective Trust was 17 against a requirement of 14, and unresolved Systemic Risk was 0. Therefore the game reached an open-continuity, non-AGI ending rather than an AGI victory or systemic-risk-exclusive ending.
confusingMoments: The distinction between the decision profile and the faction ability was easy to blur: capability_rusher shaped choices but did not grant rules text.
The no-Facility setup clarification mattered substantially; Mirevanta could not treat setup as providing a starting Facility or Power.
Negotiations generated many open, superseded, unexercised, and broken promises, making it difficult to track which promises still had operational consequences.
Power trades and temporary power allocations were easy to confuse with permanent Facility ownership or permanent Compute.
Selecting declare_agi in the final cycle did not mean AGI had been declared, because eligibility and resolution still had to be satisfied.
Audit hits and the black Systemic Risk cube were related but not identical: Audit affected players with enough Customers, while unresolved Systemic Risk governed the ending condition.
teachingChanges: I would teach the game around three separate layers: action economy, negotiation and trades, and end-of-game checks.
I would give each player a one-page resource-flow diagram showing how Research, Deploy, Fund, Build, Organize, Facilities, Power, Trust, and Mandates interact.
I would emphasize that early Customers are powerful for scoring but expose players to Audit penalties once they reach three or more.
I would explain Facilities as a timing engine: construction creates capacity only when legally built and powered, so building early can compound over several rounds.
I would distinguish selection, resolution, and completion for escalations, especially AGI declaration.
I would provide a live promise ledger with one current status per promise, hiding superseded and unexercised entries unless audit history is requested.
I would teach the ending before the first round so players understand that a high score and a desirable world outcome are separate objectives.

definingMoments: Mirevanta Works won by converting rapid research into four Customers and accumulating mandate points, reaching 19 despite three Audit hits.
Kestralyn built two powered Facilities and maintained strong compute, but never developed Capability or Customers, so its infrastructure did not translate into enough score.
Corthaven’s early and sustained Facility construction made it the strongest infrastructure rival, while its allocation-window power sale generated useful compute but limited its final score.
Loopfold AI reached three Customers and solid Capability, but lagged Mirevanta in mandate accumulation and did not convert its market position into victory.

The decisive divergence was economic: Mirevanta repeatedly deployed Customers and captured customer, capability, trust, and round-mandate points; Kestralyn mostly invested in infrastructure and research that produced no Capability.
rulesReconstruction: The game is a four-player Default Game with factions, profiles, resources, actions, Facilities, Customers, Capability, Compute, Trust, Runway, mandates, negotiations, and headlines.

Each round has three cycles. Players select from currently legal actions; negotiation and possible trades occur around action resolution, with revealed legal targets and costs determining the final choice.

Research advances Capability through revealed research targets. Deploy creates Customers from legal targets. Fund supports ventures or other revealed targets. Build constructs Facilities or generators. Organize recruits or otherwise improves the available workforce/resource base.

Facilities require construction and can be powered through the grid. The first Facility receives integrated starting-grid Power; later Facilities need available power or a purchase/trade mechanism. Powered Facilities can satisfy demand and produce infrastructure value.
Headlines are revealed over time and may modify named rules. The revealed headline, rather than the profile, is authoritative for exceptions.
Systemic Risk audits every player with at least three Customers, applying the current Era penalty. Customers therefore create both scoring opportunities and audit exposure.
Mandate points come from threshold achievements, Trust, Capability, Customers, round mandates, and certain faction abilities. Score is not simply the sum of visible resource totals.
Negotiation promises can be open, superseded, fulfilled, broken, or unexercised. A promise is not automatically a completed benefit; its exercise and resolution matter.

Faction abilities are situational actions or modifiers, not general permissions. Kestralyn’s industrial velocity and orbital-compute effects rewarded infrastructure tempo but did not substitute for Capability or Customers.
The ending is evaluated separately from victory score. AGI declarations, collective Trust, and unresolved Systemic Risk determine which World Ending qualifies.
output.winnerExplanation: Seat 0, Mirevanta Works, won with 19 points. Its capability-rusher strategy was effective because it combined research with aggressive deployment: four Customers, Capability 8, and repeated mandate triggers. Its three Audit hits reduced the advantage of expansion, but the customer and mandate income outweighed that cost. Kestralyn had better infrastructure and Compute, yet scored only 8 because it never reached Capability or Customer milestones.
output.worldEndingExplanation: The World Ending was The Plural Future. No player declared AGI, so the AGI route did not qualify. Collective Trust reached 17, exceeding the required 14, and unresolved Systemic Risk was 0, below the exclusive ceiling of 4. The result therefore preserved open continuity: society achieved the cooperation threshold without an AGI emergence or a risk-driven ending.
confusingMoments: The seat labels are easy to misread: the human was described as seat 2 while the active Kestralyn record is seat 1; the faction identity, not the prose seat label, is the reliable anchor.
A strong infrastructure position looked strategically dominant, but Facilities and Compute alone produced little score without Capability, Customers, or mandate conversion.
The first Facility’s integrated starting-grid Power made early construction unusually valuable, while later Facilities depended on power allocation and trades; that distinction was easy to lose.
Power trades and promises were separate systems. A trade could occur without being causally necessary, and an accepted or open promise did not necessarily produce a fulfilled promise.
The future timeline displayed named headlines, but the actual legal effect still depended on when each headline was revealed; seeing the timeline did not mean all effects were active from the start.
Audit exposure began at three Customers, yet the record’s audit-hit totals and scrutiny values were not intuitive from the final standings alone.
The orbital-compute movement and immediate production effects made Kestralyn’s infrastructure stronger without increasing Capability, which made the faction’s low score initially surprising.
teachingChanges: Teach the scoring economy first: infrastructure enables production, but Customers, Capability, Trust, and mandates are the main scoring channels.
Give a one-line reminder whenever a player reaches three Customers: expansion now creates recurring Audit exposure.
Separate the action sequence visibly into choose action, negotiate, resolve legal target, then apply production and scoring effects.
Show Facility state as a compact chain: built, grid-ready, powered, demand satisfied, networked, and scoring contribution.
Label every negotiation outcome explicitly as offer, accepted trade, exercised promise, fulfilled promise, broken promise, or unexercised promise.
Explain that faction abilities amplify a plan; they do not replace the faction’s missing scoring prerequisites.
At the start of each cycle, display only the currently active headline rules and distinguish them from future scheduled headlines.
Clarify seat numbering and faction ownership in every decision packet, especially when the human seat and engine-seat numbering differ.

rulesReconstruction: The game is a four-round structure with three action cycles per round, using simultaneous or ordered player choices followed by authoritative resolution.
Each cycle generally involves negotiation intent, action selection, possible trades or faction interactions, action resolution, and—when relevant—power allocation or escalation handling.
Core actions include Research, Deploy, Fund, Organize, and Build. Their legal effects depend on visible resources, cards, faction abilities, and current state.

Research advances Capability through available research targets and can stop at different thresholds. Deploy increases Customers when a legal customer target is available. Fund supports ventures or other entities. Build creates Facilities or generators. Organize develops workforce or related capacity.
Trades, promises, allocations, and faction abilities are optional stateful interactions; offers can be accepted, rejected, countered, superseded, broken, or left unexercised.
Facilities produce infrastructure benefits only when powered and otherwise may be offline at final scoring. Grid-Ready status is tracked by round and matters to final evaluation.
Audits and Systemic Risk apply the Core Rules together with the Era’s visible state and legal choices. Black cubes penalize players with at least three Customers.
Future Headlines are revealed by the game state at their scheduled points; their identities need not be known in advance.

Mandates award points when threshold, round, headline, or other conditions are satisfied. Escalations and declarations can be legal yet fail to produce their intended result if eligibility or resolution conditions are absent.
Final scoring combines the accumulated score with trust, Customers, Compute, Capability, Facilities, penalties, AGI status, mandate results, and world-ending conditions.
output.winnerExplanation: Seat 0 won with 19 points. Its balanced capability-and-market engine reached 4 Customers, 8 Capability, 4 Compute, and Trust 5, while also collecting two mandates. The decisive advantage was consistent conversion of actions into threshold-based mandate points; facilities were unnecessary because the player’s customer and capability gains outweighed the infrastructure route.
output.worldEndingExplanation: The world ended as The Plural Future. AGI did not emerge because there were no qualifying declarers. The open-continuity result means the future remained unsettled rather than being closed by an AGI or catastrophic outcome.

Explain AGI declarations as a two-step process: legal selection first, qualification and successful resolution second.

rulesReconstruction: The game is a four-player Default Game with factions, profiles, resources, actions, Facilities, Customers, Capability, Compute, Trust, Runway, mandates, negotiations, and headlines.

Each round has three cycles. Players select from currently legal actions; negotiation and possible trades occur around action resolution, with revealed legal targets and costs determining the final choice.

Research advances Capability through revealed research targets. Deploy creates Customers from legal targets. Fund supports ventures or other revealed targets. Build constructs Facilities or generators. Organize recruits or otherwise improves the available workforce/resource base.

Facilities require construction and can be powered through the grid. The first Facility receives integrated starting-grid Power; later Facilities need available power or a purchase/trade mechanism. Powered Facilities can satisfy demand and produce infrastructure value.
Headlines are revealed over time and may modify named rules. The revealed headline, rather than the profile, is authoritative for exceptions.
Systemic Risk audits every player with at least three Customers, applying the current Era penalty. Customers therefore create both scoring opportunities and audit exposure.
Mandate points come from threshold achievements, Trust, Capability, Customers, round mandates, and certain faction abilities. Score is not simply the sum of visible resource totals.
Negotiation promises can be open, superseded, fulfilled, broken, or unexercised. A promise is not automatically a completed benefit; its exercise and resolution matter.

Faction abilities are situational actions or modifiers, not general permissions. Kestralyn’s industrial velocity and orbital-compute effects rewarded infrastructure tempo but did not substitute for Capability or Customers.
The ending is evaluated separately from victory score. AGI declarations, collective Trust, and unresolved Systemic Risk determine which World Ending qualifies.

rulesReconstruction: The game is a four-round structure with three action cycles per round, using simultaneous or ordered player choices followed by authoritative resolution.
Each cycle generally involves negotiation intent, action selection, possible trades or faction interactions, action resolution, and—when relevant—power allocation or escalation handling.
Core actions include Research, Deploy, Fund, Organize, and Build. Their legal effects depend on visible resources, cards, faction abilities, and current state.

Research advances Capability through available research targets and can stop at different thresholds. Deploy increases Customers when a legal customer target is available. Fund supports ventures or other entities. Build creates Facilities or generators. Organize develops workforce or related capacity.
Trades, promises, allocations, and faction abilities are optional stateful interactions; offers can be accepted, rejected, countered, superseded, broken, or left unexercised.
Facilities produce infrastructure benefits only when powered and otherwise may be offline at final scoring. Grid-Ready status is tracked by round and matters to final evaluation.
Audits and Systemic Risk apply the Core Rules together with the Era’s visible state and legal choices. Black cubes penalize players with at least three Customers.
Future Headlines are revealed by the game state at their scheduled points; their identities need not be known in advance.

Mandates award points when threshold, round, headline, or other conditions are satisfied. Escalations and declarations can be legal yet fail to produce their intended result if eligibility or resolution conditions are absent.
Final scoring combines the accumulated score with trust, Customers, Compute, Capability, Facilities, penalties, AGI status, mandate results, and world-ending conditions.

Collective Trust reached 17, exceeding the required 14, and unresolved Systemic Risk was 0, so the cooperative plural-future condition succeeded. The open-continuity result means the future remained unsettled rather than being closed by an AGI or catastrophic outcome.

teachingChanges: Start with a compact player dashboard explaining which actions primarily generate Customers, Capability, Compute, Trust, Facilities, and mandates.
Explicitly distinguish permanent resources from temporary or round-limited resources, especially allocated Compute and trade runway.
Show a cycle timeline: negotiation, selection, trade, resolution, allocation, headline, audit, and scoring effects.
Give each promise a unique immutable identifier and display its current status plus the event that superseded or resolved it.
After every action, show the immediate state delta and whether it contributed to a mandate, objective, escalation, or world-ending condition.
Explain AGI declarations as a two-step process: legal selection first, qualification and successful resolution second.
Provide a final-scoring preview during play, including projected offline penalties, Grid-Ready treatment, and remaining world-ending requirements.
